title: Solid rod material sensitivities across static, modal and harmonic response
source: Independent axial-bar scaling laws for a fixed-load discrete rod: u is proportional to 1/E, modal frequency is proportional to sqrt(E/rho), and the fixed-load harmonic response obeys E du/dE + rho du/drho + u = 0. The guide removes lateral and rigid modes; no commercial data are used.

quantities.quantity: E times static displacement derivative divided by displacement
quantities.reason: Exact axial scaling u proportional to 1/E for the fixed-load rod; only linear algebra roundoff is allowed.
Density enters only inertia, so the static fixed-load displacement derivative is exactly zero.

quantities.quantity: 2E times modal frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: The fixed-boundary discrete eigenproblem scales K with E, giving f proportional to sqrt(E).

quantities.quantity: -2rho times modal frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: The consistent mass matrix scales with density, giving f proportional to rho to the minus one half.
Independent differentiation of the assembled dynamic equilibrium gives E du/dE + rho du/drho + u = 0 at fixed force.
The same fixed-load dynamic identity applies to the imaginary component with structural loss damping held fixed.
